raw_response:
Well, I've been farming these 6 mu for 35 years now, and it's just me since the family moved to the city. That means every decision I make, I have to be able to handle it alone — no extra hands when the wheat needs harvesting and the maize needs planting in the same week.

My wheat went in last October, like always. I used my own saved seed from the year before — it's an improved variety that's been doing well, so why pay for new seed when mine is still good? I put down about 30 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting, and now that it's April, the wheat is greening up. I already gave it the spring topdress — about 25 jin of urea per mu at jointing. The extension guy says I should use more, maybe 40 jin urea, but that's too much money upfront and honestly, my land isn't that fertile anyway — throwing more fertilizer at it doesn't always help. I know my soil. I'll irrigate three times for the wheat: the returning-green water, the jointing water, and one more at heading if it stays dry. Pumping costs money — about 30 yuan each time — so I watch the sky. If it rains enough, I skip one. I sprayed herbicide once in March because the weeds were coming up early.

For maize, it's the same 6 mu right after wheat harvest in early June. The turnaround is brutal — sometimes only three or four days. I hire the combine for wheat harvest — costs about 50 yuan per mu, but there's no way I can cut 6 mu by myself in time. As soon as the wheat is off, I shallow-till and get the maize in. I have to buy hybrid seed every year — can't save it — and I budget about 25 yuan per mu for that. I put down a base dressing of compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 25 jin per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. I only irrigate the maize twice — once if June is dry at planting, and once at flowering in August. The rest of the time I pray for rain. I spray herbicide once, maybe insecticide if I see borers.

Money is tight with just one person working. I'm aiming for about 400 jin of wheat per mu and maybe 450 jin of maize. Last year was okay, not great. I'd rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing half my crop would hurt a lot more than saving 100 yuan on inputs. But I also need to keep some cash for medicine or emergencies. It's a balancing act.
